question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{1}{X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}4x{e}^{-2x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{1}{X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{x}\cdot 4x{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2[{e}^{-2x}]_{0}^{\infty } \\  & =-2(0-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
